title: Content Negotiation
description: Use HTTP content negotiation with Accept headers to serve multiple representations and versions from a single endpoint.

data.text: Content negotiation lets a client specify the desired representation format using the Accept header. You can combine it with versioning to serve multiple API versions or formats (JSON, XML, Protobuf) from a single URL.

rows: v1 JSON with custom vendor media type

data.title: Negotiating response format and version in Express.js
data.content: Parse the Accept header and route to the appropriate serializer.

items: You have multiple response formats for the same resource (JSON, XML, Protobuf)
Clients need different representations of the same data shape
You want to evolve the schema without changing URLs
You are building a hypermedia API (HAL, JSON:API, Siren)

data.text: The most formal approach embeds the version in the vendor media type. This follows RFC 6839. The server advertises supported types in an API description endpoint.

data.title: API description endpoint listing supported media types
data.content: Clients discover available representations from the API root.

data.title: Formal media types vs custom headers
data.text: Formal media types (application/vnd.example.v2+json) are more standards-compliant but require clients to set the full Accept header. Custom headers like API-Version are simpler for SDK generation.

items.question: What if the client does not send an Accept header?
items.answer: Return the default representation (usually v1 JSON). Document this behavior clearly. Never return a 406 Not Acceptable for missing Accept headers.

items.question: Can I combine content negotiation with URL versioning?
items.answer: Avoid it. Pick one versioning strategy and one representation strategy. Combining URL versioning with media-type versioning creates three dimensions of complexity.

items.question: Does content negotiation work with OpenAPI?
items.answer: Yes. Use the content field in the response object to declare each media type and its schema. OpenAPI generators will create typed request methods for each representation.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Content negotiation is powerful for multi-format APIs but complex to operate.
Use formal vendor media types for maximum standards compliance.
Always return a default when Accept is missing.
Document supported representations in your API description.
data.takeaway: Content negotiation is the right tool when you need multiple representations of the same resource. For simple versioning, URL versioning is easier to debug and document.
